## 5. Example and import ID format

Root-namespace `operator` policy (more than 10 lines, so file-backed):

```hcl
# Generated by vault-brownfield-codifier
# Capability: policies
# Doc ref: https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs

resource "vault_policy" "operator" {
  name   = "operator"
  policy = file("${path.module}/policies/root/operator.hcl")
}
```

A short policy (10 lines or fewer) in `admin/platform`:

```hcl
resource "vault_policy" "admin_platform_platform_sre_read" {
  provider = vault.platform
  name     = "platform-sre-read"
  policy   = <<-EOT
    path "secret/data/platform/sre/*" {
      capabilities = ["read", "list"]
    }
  EOT
}
```

### Import ID (TASK-006 resolution)

Verified against the harness: the import `id` is the bare policy name, relative
to the namespace of the provider alias the resource uses. Never prefix the
namespace (`admin/namespace-admin` is wrong).

| Namespace | Import `id` |
|---|---|
| root | `operator` |
| `admin` | `namespace-admin` |
| `admin/platform` | `platform-sre-read` (resource uses `provider = vault.<alias>`) |

EGP/RGP use `vault_egp_policy` / `vault_rgp_policy` with the bare name as import ID (verified, `task-s01-decision.md`).
Each goes in `<ns>_sentinel.tf` with `policy = file("${path.module}/policies/sentinel/<ns>/<kind>-<name>.sentinel")`.
A namespace without any gets no file and `coverage.md` records "none".
